info.description: A source: patients (or customers) walk in at a rate that follows an arrival schedule, so a morning peak and a quiet afternoon are one record rather than a hand-built expression. The schedule's values are arrivals per minute and drive a non-homogeneous Poisson process; edit them in the model's Schedules tab. No input port -- this asset starts the flow. To stamp a service target on every arrival, chain the Service target asset after it.

info.description: Classify an arriving patient into one of three acuity classes by probability and stamp entity.acuity (1 = most urgent) and entity.priority (= acuity, so a LowestValueFirst resource downstream serves the most urgent first). One exit: a single stream with priority set is more composable than three physically separate paths, since most triage feeds one shared queue rather than three.

info.description: A service desk where customers balk (leave immediately) if too many are already waiting, and renege (give up) if they wait past their patience. Exits: 'served' (got helped) and 'left' (balked or reneged, entity.left_reason says which).

info.description: A visit that needs BOTH a room and a clinician: the patient holds one clinician from the named pool for the whole visit and one of this instance's own rooms. The room queues FIFO by default; to serve by entity.priority (e.g. set upstream by Triage), give this instance's own room resource a LowestValueFirst discipline with ranking_expr entity.priority in the model's Resources tab -- not the default, since an entity with no priority ever assigned would otherwise fail there. An emergency already in a room is not interrupted: preemption needs one block to own the whole hold, and here the clinician and the room are held across two (ARCHITECTURE 5.17 scope).

info.title: Walk-in clinic (library assets)
info.description: One 10-hour day of a walk-in clinic, built entirely from the Services and healthcare library. Walk-ins arrive on a time-of-day schedule (two peaks, about 125 patients), Triage stamps an acuity class and priority, a service target stamps a 45-minute due date, a one-person registration desk models balking and reneging (its 'left' exit is left-without-being-seen) and a consultation room -- a room plus a clinician -- serves the registered patients most-urgent-first. A clinic day is a TERMINATING simulation, so it runs with no warm-up: the quiet start and the end-of-day tail are part of the answer, not transient error to discard.
